title.narrative: OVOF - Use of Art, Media, and Culture-Uganda

description.narrative: OVOF has seen the results of working with artists, media and cultural workers. It helps shiftmental models around gender and sexuality, and disrupts stigma steeped in bias andprejudice. OVOF partners have (effectively) used art and arts-based public campaigns (forexample, film festivals) to change the way people think about highly stigmatised topics suchas sex work, both within feminist movements and in society. Art has the power to reachpeople beyond activist circles and across country borders. Shifting social norms aroundgender and sexuality (both within and outside movements) is critical to OVOF and its workwith artists.

APC aims to do 1 intervention in Uganda which looks to build capacity around the use of art, media, and culture by using digital technologies to visibilise alternative narratives of structurally silenced women and their communities.

APC partners organised 1 intervention in Uganda around the use of art, media, and culture. These were in the form of digital storytelling workshops where participants produced audio visual stories to share their narratives, and also in the form of content creation workshops where participants created content on queerness, gender, sexuality etc. using different kinds of art and writing.

APC aims to do 2 interventions in Uganda which looks to build capacity around the use of art, media, and culture by using digital technologies to visibilise alternative narratives of structurally silenced women and their communities.

Partners in Uganda are using art, media, and culture in creative ways to talk about SSW and communities and their rights and tell their stories. Technology plays a very significant role in this. Digital storytelling, creative content jams, pot-painting, and creating audio-visual content are all activities implemented under the OVOF project.
